name: Traffic White
lede: Traffic White is a faintly green-tinted white from the German RAL signage standard, used for lane markings and signs.

sections.title: A road-marking white
sections.body:
RAL, founded in 1927, lists this hue as RAL 9016, a screen approximation of that spec [1]. The ISCC-NBS language for its block calls it a greenish white, a faint cast of only a few LCH units that most eyes would read as plain white [1]. The books give no account of why RAL's white carries this particular tint rather than a neutral one, so that choice is undocumented [1].

Its nearest named neighbor in our library is [[mint-cream]], very slightly warmer [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this hue, as photographed, in 360 of 23,781 paintings (1.51 percent), more common than 75 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks sharply in the 1300s, at 6.7 times the expected rate for the 251 paintings we have from that century [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 70 percent of its 259 occurrences[2].

[[painter:gerard-de-lairesse|Gerard de Lairesse]] is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 4 of 28 of his works, 7.0 times his home museums' baseline [2]. It is most over-represented in paintings from China, at 2.4 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest matching painting is dated 960, 967 years before RAL recorded the standard in 1927, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
